title: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2607.16235v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Mobile and wearable devices offer an unprecedented opportunity for continuous, passive health monitoring and active health coaching. However, the largest wearable datasets are proprietary, and leading wearable foundation models trained on them are rarely open weight or include reproducible training code. To accelerate open science in wearable health, we introduce OpenMyHeartCounts (OpenMHC), the largest and most comprehensive wearable health dataset broadly accessible to qualified researchers, alongside open-source implementations and weights for recent wearable foundation models. Derived from over a decade of data collected through the My Heart Counts study app, OpenMHC comprises over 67M participant-hours of wearable recordings across up to 19 sensor channels (e.g., step count, heart rate, sleep, workouts) and up to 170 health, lifestyle, mood, and behavioral variables from 11,894 participants. translated_title: OpenMHC：加速可穿戴基础模型的科学发展
translated_abstract: 移动和可穿戴设备为持续、被动式的健康监测和主动健康指导提供了前所未有的机会。然而，目前最大的可穿戴数据集均为专有数据，基于这些数据训练的领先可穿戴基础模型很少开放权重或包含可复现的训练代码。为了加速可穿戴健康领域的开放科学，我们推出了OpenMyHeartCounts（OpenMHC），这是面向合格研究人员开放的最大、最全面的可穿戴健康数据集，同时提供近期可穿戴基础模型的开源实现和权重。OpenMHC源自通过My Heart Counts研究应用收集的十余年数据，包含来自11,894名参与者的超过6700万参与者小时的可穿戴记录，涵盖多达19个传感器通道（如步数、心率、睡眠、锻炼）以及多达170个健康、生活方式、情绪和行为变量。此外，我们还建立了一个……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发布了OpenMHC——目前面向研究人员开放的最大、最全面的可穿戴健康数据集（涵盖11,894名参与者、超过6700万小时记录、最多19个传感器通道和170个健康行为变量），并配套提供可穿戴基础模型的开源实现与模型权重，以推动可穿戴健康领域的开放科学。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces OpenMHC, the largest and most comprehensive openly accessible wearable health dataset (over 67M participant-hours from 11,894 participants, up to 19 sensor channels and 170 variables), along with open-source implementations and weights of wearable foundation models, to accelerate open science in wearable health.
